title: Summary of Empowerment (Sekoddeśa; Tib. dbang mdor bstan pa), Toh 361
author: Indian Buddhist tantra, held to be a section of the lost Kālacakra root tantra (Paramādibuddha); introduction draws on Nāropa's Sekoddeśaṭīkā
translator: Vienna Buddhist Translation Studies Group (Klaus-Dieter Mathes et al.) for 84000: Translating the Words of the Buddha
year: c. 11th century text; English first published 2020
edition_cited: 84000 online edition, first published 2020-04-14; file read is v 1.2.22 (2025), CC BY-NC-ND
locator_hints: Translators' introduction, section 'Sixfold Yoga': list of the four night signs and six day signs with Sanskrit and Tibetan terms; Nāropa's gloss

The Translation, verses 24-34: withdrawal and absorption; the ten signs; 'With eyes neither closed nor open'; the reflection seen in the cloudless sky; the simile of the virgin seeing an image in a divination mirror
verses 35-76: wind control and death signs; verses 77-92: the last three limbs
summary: The root verse text for the Kālacakra six-limbed yoga, in a free scholarly translation with introduction. The introduction explains that in the first limb, withdrawal, the senses are turned from outer objects to 'reflections of emptiness', which appear as signs: at night smoke, mirage, firefly and lamp; by day flame, moon, sun, darkness, digit of the moon and great drop. The verses state that the signs are seen with eyes neither closed nor open, in the sky, as something neither imagined nor an outer object, and compare the seeing to a girl seeing an image appear in a divination mirror. The second limb applies five mental factors to the signs once they have appeared. The remaining limbs concern winds, drops and bliss. The verses are terse; method is mostly left to commentary.
why_relevant: Primary source for the sequence of perceived signs in Kālacakra withdrawal yoga, with the eye instruction and the explicit statement that the appearances are seen and are not constructed images; freely published by the translators.

Summary kept to the level of the translators' own public summary and introduction. Later sections concern sexual yoga and are outside this library's question. The 'darkness' day-sign is elsewhere rendered Rāhu or 'black'. Saved file is the TEI stripped to text; verse numbers are in braces.
